sections.html:
Brighton lies just southeast of Rochester in Monroe County. A sale involves two offices: Building and Planning for zoning paperwork, and the county clerk for recording the deed. The 2025 estimate is 36,695 residents, slightly below the 37,137 counted in 2020.

Among 15,988 households, 56.4% own their homes. Median value is $282,100 and median gross rent is $1,350, while owners spend a median of $2,055 monthly with a mortgage or $935 with none. An owner of many years may find that a buyer prices in updates, so check what neighbors' houses sold for, and in what shape, before you set a number.

Brighton has no central village. Rochester annexed the old village of Brighton, around East Avenue and Winton Road, in 1905. The commercial hub is Twelve Corners, where Winton Road, Monroe Avenue and Elmwood Avenue cross, and Brighton High School and Twelve Corners Middle School stand there.

  • The Erie Canal runs through town, along with the Erie Canal Heritage Trail.
  • Lynch Woods Nature Park gives access to the Lehigh Valley Trail.
  • The Brickyard Trail park, built on a former clay-mining site, opened in 2017.

Name the trails and parks in your listing. Buyers like to know what is within walking distance.

sections.h2: Do you need a certificate of occupancy to sell?
sections.html:
Not at a sale. Building and Planning issues no Certificate of Occupancy when ownership transfers. What it offers instead is a Zoning Verification Letter, which buyers and lenders ask for at a sale or refinance.

The letter names the property's legal use and its zoning district, and lists any violations the office knows of. Either you or the buyer's attorney can order it with the form on the town website.

sections.h2: Working with the Building and Planning office
sections.html:
• The department is part of Public Works. It enforces the state's Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code, and the town adds its own sprinkler rules.
  • Planning staff also support the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, Conservation Board, Architectural Review Board and Historic Preservation Commission.
  • Certificate of Compliance requests count as land use applications, and permits are filed online in the town's OpenGov portal.
  • Payments are taken in person, by phone or by mailed check. Online payment is not offered.

Town Hall at 2300 Elmwood Avenue closed for renovation in November 2024, and town offices have been working from 680 Westfall Road. Call the town to confirm the current office location before you drop anything off, and ask which window handles the request you are making.

sections.h2: Property tax bills and help for owners in trouble
sections.html:
One tax office in town handles both the town and county bill and the school tax bill. The town website has forms to request a bill, a past receipt, or a change to the mailing address and mortgage information. The first installment of town and county tax is due February 10, and the tax clerk suggests treating January 31 as the real date.

Seller and buyer divide the tax bill at closing. Before signing a contract, ask for the current bill and a receipt for payments made. Receipts for earlier years come through the same page.

Owners behind on a mortgage can call the HOPP hotline, 1-855-466-3456, listed on the town's tax page, or visit homeownerhelpny.com for a referral to a legal services or housing counseling organization. It exists so that no New York family loses a home for lack of a lawyer or counselor.

Brighton deeds are recorded by the Monroe County Clerk at 39 West Main Street in Rochester. To get same-day recording, be in line by 4:30 pm. Later drop-offs are handled the next day. A deed needs an original signature, a notary acknowledgment, a full legal description, and the new tax number.

Monroe County Clerk charges on a residential deed
Document or chargeAmount
One-page deed$50, plus $5 for each added page
TP-584 transfer tax form$5
RP-5217 equalization form (residential)$125
Extra fee on residential deeds$10
Transfer tax$4 per $1,000 of price

Sellers normally cover the transfer tax, and buyers of residences at $1 million or more add a 1% extra tax. A free Restrictive Covenant Modification form has been available since June 3, 2026, for removing unlawful discriminatory covenants from recorded documents. Ask your title company whether anything of that kind sits on your deed.

1. Request a Zoning Verification Letter through the town website so the legal use and zoning district are on paper.
  2. Request your current tax bill and proof of payment from the tax office, with earlier years' receipts if a buyer wants them.
  3. Get a payoff figure from your lender. Behind on payments? Phone the HOPP hotline before anything else.
  4. Sign a contract. The deed is drawn up with your original signature, a notary acknowledgment, the full legal description and the new tax number.
  5. Take the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 downtown to the Monroe County Clerk with the fees listed above.

With a financed buyer, expect an appraisal and inspection requests before the contract is final. A cash buyer uses the same papers without waiting on a lender, so your own schedule can set the closing once title is clear.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Brighton house
sections.html:
You can list, sell privately or accept a cash purchase. Tidy houses are easy to market. Homes needing work, rentals with tenants and inherited properties often go faster to a cash buyer who accepts them as is.

Compare any cash offer with your likely net from listing, after repairs, agent fees and the taxes and utilities you would carry for months. Either way, keep the Zoning Verification Letter and a current tax bill in your paperwork, because every buyer asks about legal use and tax status.

faqs.q: Does Brighton issue a certificate of occupancy when a house sells?
faqs.a: Not at a sale. Building and Planning hands out Zoning Verification Letters instead, which give legal use, zoning district and known violations.

faqs.q: Which office files a Brighton deed?
faqs.a: The Monroe County Clerk in downtown Rochester. Recording costs $50 for a single page and $5 for each page added, and the TP-584 and RP-5217 go in with it. Get there by 4:30 pm to finish the same day.

faqs.q: When is the first installment of Brighton town and county tax due?
faqs.a: February 10, though the tax clerk advises paying by January 31. School tax comes on a separate bill, and the town website offers forms to request bills and past receipts.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will I pay in Brighton?
faqs.a: Monroe County charges $4 for every $1,000 of price, usually paid by the seller. A further 1% applies to residences at $1 million or more, and the buyer pays that.

faqs.q: Where do I go if I need help avoiding foreclosure in Brighton?
faqs.a: Dial the HOPP hotline, 1-855-466-3456, or go to homeownerhelpny.com. Both point owners toward a nearby legal services or housing counseling group, and the town's tax page links to them.
